blocks.text: The reality of property manager burnout

The profession is defined by constant interruptions. You balance tenant requests, landlord demands, and contractor schedules. This environment leads to chronic stress. Research shows 53% of property managers report mental health issues. The nature of the work is reactive. You often feel you lack control over your own schedule.

Burnout is not just about having too much to do. It is about how the work is structured. You absorb frustration from stakeholders. You also handle sensitive financial and compliance tasks. This requires high emotional labor. When you lack clear boundaries, you cannot switch off. You carry the mental load of every open maintenance request home with you.

items: Relentless reactivity where emergencies override your planned work.
Manual data entry that keeps you tethered to the computer.
Lack of clear delegation for routine approvals.
Verbal abuse from stakeholders that drives exhaustion.

blocks.text: Practical fixes for your daily routine

You do not need expensive software to start feeling better. Start by reclaiming your attention. Use the Focus app on your Mac to block distracting sites during deep work sessions. Use Be Focused to run a Pomodoro timer. This forces you to take breaks. It prevents the accumulation of stress throughout the day.

If you are struggling with work-related stress, follow your employer's policy on mental health resources. Seek clinical support if you feel overwhelmed. These tools are for productivity, not medical treatment.
